title: A house built on five
told: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? what’s one thing that holds up your week, something you’d really miss if it went?
options: keep them in mind. today is about what holds a life up.
good. today, five that have held people up for centuries.
that’s okay. here are five to look at.

steps.line: ‘Umar remembered a day in Medina, sitting with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, when a stranger walked in, his clothes brilliant white, his hair very black.
There was no dust of travel on him, yet no one knew him. He sat knee to knee with the Prophet ﷺ and asked, “Tell me about Islam.”

steps.q: No one in the room knows this man. Who do you think he turns out to be?
o: A companion in disguise, testing them
steps.why: Jibril, Gabriel, the angel who brought the Qur’an. Watch how he teaches without giving a single lesson.

steps.line: Bear witness that there is no god but God and Muhammad is His messenger. Pray. Give zakat. Fast Ramadan. Make the pilgrimage, if you are able.
“You have spoken truly,” the stranger said. And the companions sitting there were amazed.

steps.q: No dust of travel on him, yet no one in Medina knew him. Why was that so strange?
o: Strangers weren’t let into the mosque
He hadn’t come far, yet wasn’t from town
steps.why: A traveler would be dusty; a local would be known. He was neither. Then came the strangest part, ‘Umar said: “he asked him, and then told him he was right.”

steps.line: He asked about faith, and about worshipping God as if you see Him, then left. It was the angel Jibril, the Prophet ﷺ said, come to teach them their religion.
Another saying puts it in one picture: Islam is built on five. Like a house, held up by its pillars.

steps.q: Zakat is a yearly gift from savings you’ve held for a year. How much is it, usually?
steps.why: On savings above a set minimum, the nisab, the usual rate is 2.5%. Shia teaching adds khums, a fifth of some gains. Sunni and Shia teaching draw the same house a little differently.

steps.line: Today the five keep different clocks. The witness, always. Prayer, every day. Zakat and the fast, every year. The pilgrimage, once in a life.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Your health or money will never allow the trip to Mecca. Have you failed a pillar?
o: Yes, until you find a way to go
Yes, unless you fast extra days
No: it’s asked only of those able
steps.why: The Qur’an asks hajj of those “able to find a way.” It also says God burdens no soul beyond what it can bear.

say: here’s what i love. the answer that holds up a whole faith fit into one breath. five things.
in islam, the pillars hold up a house you live in, not boxes you tick. and the house fits the person: the qur’an asks the pilgrimage only of those able to make the journey.

steps.q: Jibril’s last question was about ihsan, doing what is beautiful. The answer: worship God as if you see Him. And if you can’t?
o: Then remember that He sees you
Then keep at it until you can
steps.why: “…and if you do not see Him, He sees you.” Many Muslims hold ihsan as the highest of the hadith’s three levels: islam, iman, ihsan.

today.say: today, learn the five by name, one on each finger: shahada, salat, zakat, sawm, hajj. then, if you like, ask a muslim friend which pillar holds them up most.
options: lovely. five fingers, one hand, one house.
beautiful. that question opens real conversations.

sources: Sahih Muslim 8 (the hadith of Jibril, narrated by ‘Umar: a man with very white clothes and very black hair, no trace of travel, known to none; he sat with his knees against the Prophet’s knees; “Tell me about Islam”; the five; “You have spoken truly”; “we were amazed that he asked him and then confirmed him”; questions on iman, ihsan and the Hour; “It was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion”)
Sahih al-Bukhari 50 (a shorter version of the same hadith, from Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 8; Sahih Muslim 16 (Islam is built on five)
Qur’an 3:97 (pilgrimage for those able to make the journey)
Shia teaching: usul al-din and furu‘ al-din (roots and branches of religion)
check: Iman and ihsan are summarized as “faith, and worshipping God as if you see Him”; the questions about the Hour and its signs are left out. In Muslim 8 the Prophet ﷺ tells ‘Umar who it was some days later; the caption keeps it short. Confirm.
Painting PL2 shows a white light at the doorway for the stranger, no figure. Confirm it is fine to suggest Jibril’s arrival as light.
Shot 5 says “every year” for zakat and the fast; zakat is due after a lunar year on savings above the threshold. Confirm the simplification.
Painting PL5 shows today’s Kaaba with pilgrims small and far away. Confirm.
